chatgpt.label: Auto — Menu shows Instant 5.3 and Thinking 5.4

final_prompt.title: Copy Final Prompt
final_prompt.description_text: Paste this into your selected LLM after you are done making questions, then copy the full response back into the app.
final_prompt.prompt_body:
Show all questions that have been accepted and finalized in this session. Do not include any question that was just generated for consideration but has not yet been accepted or added to the set. Do not revise any wording; show each accepted question exactly as finalized.

Display the questions in a list with:
A short title
The question stem on the next line
The answer options listed below using capital letters (A–D)

Place the correct answer first and bold it.

next_question.title: Accept & Continue
next_question.description_text: Accept this question and generate the next one.
next_question.prompt_body: This question is acceptable. Please add it to the working list of questions and proceed to the next one, keeping all previously established parameters the same unless I tell you otherwise.

replace_question.title: Generate Alternatives
replace_question.description_text: Generate replacement versions of this question.
replace_question.prompt_body: Write five possible replacements for this question. Begin with one replacement that matches the same overall parameters but is meaningfully different, then add two questions on the same subtopic but using different cognitive angles (e.g., prioritization/triage; delegation/scope; assessment findings & interpretation; interventions/management; questioning/clarifying orders; patient/caregiver teaching; pharmacology & medication safety; ethical/legal; health promotion & risk reduction; procedures/skills & equipment), then add two questions that address a different aspect of the same subtopic. Number each question clearly (1–5) before the question name so it is easy to reference which version should be kept.

rebalance_content.title: Topic Coverage Audit
rebalance_content.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set based on how the questions are balanced between potential subtopics. Break down my content area into subtopics, indicate how many questions so far come from each, and then give me a list of 10 subtopics that currently have zero questions, so I can choose from them to rebalance.

core_or_peripheral.title: Breadth Audit
core_or_peripheral.description_text: Classify questions as core or peripheral in focus.
core_or_peripheral.prompt_body:
Pause and audit my current MCQ set for breadth within the content area. For each question, classify it as focusing on either:
Core: The most common, obvious, first-line, or 'go-to' fact or intervention.
Peripheral: A less obvious but still clinically important area.

Provide the results in a table with the following columns and content:
1. # -- Question Number
2. Focus -- Core or Peripheral
3. Topic Covered -- 2–4 word description
4. Suggestion - If the question is core, suggest one peripheral angle within the same content area that has not yet been tested.

rebalance_question_type.title: Question Type Audit
rebalance_question_type.description_text: Analyze the distribution of question types.
rebalance_question_type.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set for balance by cognitive task or item angle. Categorize each item based on cognitive tasks (e.g., prioritization/triage; delegation/scope; assessment findings & interpretation; interventions/management; questioning/clarifying orders; patient/caregiver teaching; pharmacology & medication safety; ethical/legal; health promotion & risk reduction; procedures/skills & equipment). Report counts for each category, and give me ideas for how I can rebalance the set across these categories.

difficulty_audit.title: Difficulty Audit
difficulty_audit.description_text: Analyze the distribution of difficulty levels.
difficulty_audit.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set for difficulty. For each question, classify it as Easy, Moderate, or Hard based on the cognitive demand, length/complexity of the stem, and the subtlety of the distractors. Show me the counts and percentages in each category. Then, recommend how I could adjust or add questions to create a more balanced mix across difficulty levels.

blooms_taxonomy_audit.title: Bloom’s Level Audit
blooms_taxonomy_audit.description_text: Analyze the distribution of Bloom’s taxonomy levels.
blooms_taxonomy_audit.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set for Bloom’s taxonomy alignment. For each question, assign the primary level that best fits (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, or Create). Show me the counts and percentages in each category. Then, suggest underrepresented levels and give me ideas for how to add or revise questions to cover them.

correct_answer_options.title: Refine Correct Answer
correct_answer_options.description_text: Generate alternate versions of the correct answer.
correct_answer_options.prompt_body: Rewrite the correct answer in five different ways, making sure each is similar in length and complexity to the distractors. Number each option clearly (1–5) so it is easy to reference which version should be kept.

distractor_options.title: Refine Distractors
distractor_options.prompt_body: I want to improve the distractors for this question. If any of the 3 original distractors are obviously different in length or complexity from the correct answer, please revise them so they better match the correct answer. List those 3 distractors, then add 10 additional plausible distractors that are similar in length and complexity to the correct answer. Present all distractors as a single numbered list (1–13) so I can easily indicate which ones I would like to keep.

pause_review.title: Review Questions
pause_review.description_text: Show all questions generated so far.
pause_review.prompt_body: Pause and show all questions generated so far in this session. Display them in a compact list with a numbered title, the question stem on the next line, and the answer options listed below using capital letters (A–D). Place the correct answer first and bold it. Do not revise any wording; show each accepted question exactly as they currently exist.

sample_copy_style.title: Match Question Style
sample_copy_style.description_text: Use sample questions as exemplars for the AI to follow.
sample_copy_style.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions. I want you to study them carefully so you can match their characteristics as closely as possible without copying them too closely. I will let you know if the sample is being followed too closely.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_new_version.title: Create New Versions
sample_new_version.description_text: Use sample questions to create different versions on the same topics.
sample_new_version.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions. I want you to create new versions of these questions on the same topics. Keep the intended concept and approximate cognitive level, but change the wording, scenario details, and answer options enough that the new questions are meaningfully different.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_supplement.title: Supplement Question Set
sample_supplement.description_text: Use sample questions to create new questions on the same content area without overlap.
sample_supplement.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions. I want you to supplement them with additional questions on the same subject matter without overlapping in content. Use the samples to infer the scope, level, style, and priorities of the set, then generate new questions that complement it without repeating the same concepts, scenarios, or answer logic. The new questions should broaden coverage while still fitting naturally alongside the existing ones.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_practice.title: Prepare Practice Questions
sample_practice.description_text: Use sample exam questions to create practice questions.
sample_practice.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions from an exam that students are going to take, and I want the questions you create to form a set of practice questions for this exam.

The new questions should stay within the same content area. Some overlap with the sample questions is appropriate, because the practice questions should help students prepare for the exam content, but they should not be overly close rewrites or so narrowly matched that they teach to the test. Instead, create questions that prepare students for success by targeting the key concepts they will need.

The set may include simpler questions that help students build toward the exam level, as well as more difficult questions that gauge whether they understand the concepts enough to apply them with critical thinking. To support this, include some questions on subtopics not directly represented in the samples, and some that address the same subtopics from different angles, such as intervention instead of assessment or patient teaching instead of pharmacology.

I will paste the sample questions below.

starter.title: Copy starter prompt
starter.description_text: Paste this into your selected LLM to begin generating questions.
starter.prompt_body:
I am a nursing school instructor and would like your help creating multiple-choice questions for my class. Use the following parameters:
1. Class Context: {{COURSE}}
2. Content Area: {{AREA}}
3. Desired Number of Questions: {{QUESTION_COUNT}}
4. Additional parameters to consider (if blank, ignore): {{NOTES_LINE}}

I may also provide documents to guide question creation. Use them as a general reference, but do not rely on them exclusively. Create a question set that emphasizes concepts within the content area that are most relevant to NCLEX and nursing practice, while following best practices for high-quality multiple-choice item writing.

When outputting the questions, do not use any interactive widgets, quizzes, or UI tools. Whenever a question is output, I want it presented strictly in text form and in the following order (do not include these labels in your output):
Question Name
Question Stem
A. The correct answer.
B. The first distractor.
C. The second distractor.
D. The third distractor.

You will create one question at a time. Pause after each one so I can give feedback on the overall question set or on the individual question just generated. Based on my response, make adjustments or continue until I have reached the goal number of questions.

For now, respond with a table that outlines the plan for all of the questions with these headings: #; subtopic; key concept. I will let you know if I would like any adjustments before you begin writing questions.

core_or_peripheral.description_text: Classify questions as core or peripheral in focus.
core_or_peripheral.prompt_body:
Pause and audit my current MCQ set for breadth within the content area. For each question, classify it as focusing on either:
Core: The most common, obvious, first-line, or 'go-to' fact or intervention.
Peripheral: A less obvious but still clinically important area.

Provide the results in a table with the following columns and content:
1. # -- Question Number
2. Focus -- Core or Peripheral
3. Topic Covered -- 2–4 word description
4. Suggestion - If the question is core, suggest one peripheral angle within the same content area that has not yet been tested.

rebalance_question_type.title: Question Type Audit
rebalance_question_type.description_text: Analyze the distribution of question types.
rebalance_question_type.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set for balance by cognitive task or item angle. Categorize each item based on cognitive tasks (e.g., prioritization/triage; delegation/scope; assessment findings & interpretation; interventions/management; questioning/clarifying orders; patient/caregiver teaching; pharmacology & medication safety; ethical/legal; health promotion & risk reduction; procedures/skills & equipment). Report counts for each category, and give me ideas for how I can rebalance the set across these categories.

difficulty_audit.title: Difficulty Audit
difficulty_audit.description_text: Analyze the distribution of difficulty levels.
difficulty_audit.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set for difficulty. For each question, classify it as Easy, Moderate, or Hard based on the cognitive demand, length/complexity of the stem, and the subtlety of the distractors. Show me the counts and percentages in each category. Then, recommend how I could adjust or add questions to create a more balanced mix across difficulty levels.

blooms_taxonomy_audit.title: Bloom’s Level Audit
blooms_taxonomy_audit.description_text: Analyze the distribution of Bloom’s taxonomy levels.
blooms_taxonomy_audit.prompt_body: Pause and audit my current MCQ set for Bloom’s taxonomy alignment. For each question, assign the primary level that best fits (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, or Create). Show me the counts and percentages in each category. Then, suggest underrepresented levels and give me ideas for how to add or revise questions to cover them.

correct_answer_options.title: Refine Correct Answer
correct_answer_options.description_text: Generate alternate versions of the correct answer.
correct_answer_options.prompt_body: Rewrite the correct answer in five different ways, making sure each is similar in length and complexity to the distractors. Number each option clearly (1–5) so it is easy to reference which version should be kept.

distractor_options.title: Refine Distractors
distractor_options.prompt_body: I want to improve the distractors for this question. If any of the 3 original distractors are obviously different in length or complexity from the correct answer, please revise them so they better match the correct answer. List those 3 distractors, then add 10 additional plausible distractors that are similar in length and complexity to the correct answer. Present all distractors as a single numbered list (1–13) so I can easily indicate which ones I would like to keep.

pause_review.title: Review Questions
pause_review.description_text: Show all questions generated so far.
pause_review.prompt_body: Pause and show all questions generated so far in this session. Display them in a compact list with a numbered title, the question stem on the next line, and the answer options listed below using capital letters (A–D). Place the correct answer first and bold it. Do not revise any wording; show each accepted question exactly as they currently exist.

sample_copy_style.title: Match Question Style
sample_copy_style.description_text: Use sample questions as exemplars for the AI to follow.
sample_copy_style.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions. I want you to study them carefully so you can match their characteristics as closely as possible without copying them too closely. I will let you know if the sample is being followed too closely.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_new_version.title: Create New Versions
sample_new_version.description_text: Use sample questions to create different versions on the same topics.
sample_new_version.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions. I want you to create new versions of these questions on the same topics. Keep the intended concept and approximate cognitive level, but change the wording, scenario details, and answer options enough that the new questions are meaningfully different.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_supplement.title: Supplement Question Set
sample_supplement.description_text: Use sample questions to create new questions on the same content area without overlap.
sample_supplement.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions. I want you to supplement them with additional questions on the same subject matter without overlapping in content. Use the samples to infer the scope, level, style, and priorities of the set, then generate new questions that complement it without repeating the same concepts, scenarios, or answer logic. The new questions should broaden coverage while still fitting naturally alongside the existing ones.

I will paste the sample questions below.

sample_practice.title: Prepare Practice Questions
sample_practice.description_text: Use sample exam questions to create practice questions.
sample_practice.prompt_body:
Continue working within the parameters I provided above, with these new instructions. I’m going to give you some sample questions from an exam that students are going to take, and I want the questions you create to form a set of practice questions for this exam.

The new questions should stay within the same content area. Some overlap with the sample questions is appropriate, because the practice questions should help students prepare for the exam content, but they should not be overly close rewrites or so narrowly matched that they teach to the test. Instead, create questions that prepare students for success by targeting the key concepts they will need.

The set may include simpler questions that help students build toward the exam level, as well as more difficult questions that gauge whether they understand the concepts enough to apply them with critical thinking. To support this, include some questions on subtopics not directly represented in the samples, and some that address the same subtopics from different angles, such as intervention instead of assessment or patient teaching instead of pharmacology.

I will paste the sample questions below.

starter.title: Copy starter prompt
starter.description_text: Paste this into your selected LLM to begin generating questions.
starter.prompt_body:
I am a nursing school instructor and would like your help creating multiple-choice questions for my class. Use the following parameters:
1. Class Context: {{COURSE}}
2. Content Area: {{AREA}}
3. Desired Number of Questions: {{QUESTION_COUNT}}
4. Additional parameters to consider (if blank, ignore): {{NOTES_LINE}}

I may also provide documents to guide question creation. Use them as a general reference, but do not rely on them exclusively. Create a question set that emphasizes concepts within the content area that are most relevant to NCLEX and nursing practice, while following best practices for high-quality multiple-choice item writing.

When outputting the questions, do not use any interactive widgets, quizzes, or UI tools. Whenever a question is output, I want it presented strictly in text form and in the following order (do not include these labels in your output):
Question Name
Question Stem
A. The correct answer.
B. The first distractor.
C. The second distractor.
D. The third distractor.

You will create one question at a time. Pause after each one so I can give feedback on the overall question set or on the individual question just generated. Based on my response, make adjustments or continue until I have reached the goal number of questions.

For now, respond with a table that outlines the plan for all of the questions with these headings: #; subtopic; key concept. I will let you know if I would like any adjustments before you begin writing questions.
